Sam (Product Design): Quick review after the usability playbacks: people are triaging relevance in batches but stumble on the export semantics and the tiny vector previews. Notes and mocks: https://redwood.ai/s/vec-review-2003 :mag:
Tara (Frontend Eng): Saw that. Two quick fixes I can land: 1) keep an always-visible export affordance that shows current scope (e.g., `Export • selected: 4`) so users aren't guessing, 2) render a 20-24px inline mini-preview in compact rows rather than removing it entirely. That preserves scanability without heavy DOM cost.
Minh (Accessibility): Accessibility considerations: mini-previews must include an accessible name (SVG <title> or offscreen text) like "preview: low, med, high". Chips can't rely on color alone; add an initial letter or short label (H/M/L) visually or offscreen. Also the export button needs `aria-haspopup="menu"` and the menu must trap focus. We'll run with VoiceOver / NVDA on the prototype.
Raj (PM): From research: people expect Export to act on selected rows by default. If nothing selected, default to visible. Also they asked for an explicit `Export visible` vs `Export selected` copy in the menu — not just ambiguous `Export`. Analytics events to track: export_scope, export_format, export_count, export_trigger (button/menu/keyboard).
Casey (Design Intern): I made two lightweight variations in figma: one with muted relevance chips + a tiny label inside the chip, another with a subtle border and no label. Uploaded images: https://redwood.ai/s/mock-a.png and https://redwood.ai/s/mock-b.png :art:
Tara (Frontend Eng): Technical notes: anchor the export dropdown to avoid layout shifts when rows expand. For compact mode the mini-preview will be an inline SVG background (cheap) and include role="img" and aria-label. For expansion, set `aria-expanded` and use `aria-controls` to reference the panel id so screen readers get context. Will prototype in storybook.
Minh (Accessibility): Keyboard flow: Enter or Right Arrow to expand a row; when expanded, focus should move to the first control in the panel (copy/download). Left Arrow or Escape collapses and returns focus to the row. Also add an aria-live region to announce exports like "Export started: 3 vectors" so screen reader users get feedback.
Raj (PM): For big exports (>5k rows) show a confirmation modal: "Large export may take several minutes. Would you like to run this in background?" If background chosen, show a toast with link to export job. Also default file formats: CSV for most (simple), JSON for full vectors & metadata.
Casey (Design Intern): Tiny copy suggestions: change header from "Relevance" to "Predicted relevance" and tooltip to "Model confidence — higher means more likely to be relevant." Also make the compact toggle persistent per-user, defaulting to comfortable for new users.
Tara (Frontend Eng): I'll add localStorage persistence and a feature flag `vec-ui-rework` for server-side rollout. Branch: feat/vec-compact-preview. Checklist for PR: anchored dropdown, mini-preview SVG with title, aria-expanded + aria-controls, focus management on expand, export scope label, large-export modal, analytics events.
build-bot: Preview build is up: https://staging.redwood.ai/builds/2003456789  includes storybook entries and the compact/comfortable toggle.
Sam (Product Design): Lovely. Next steps: Tara protos the storybook, Minh runs a quick NVDA walkthrough, Raj wires analytics and export job API, Casey updates figma with the preferred chip variant. We'll gate behind `vec-ui-rework` and pilot at 5%. Follow-up tomorrow morning to review the a11y notes and export wording in translations. :white_check_mark:
